chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah from 'Umar ibn Yazid, that he heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

"Indeed, in the night there is an hour that a Muslim servant does not meet while praying and supplicating to Allah in it, except that He answers him every night." I said, "May Allah make you perfect, which hour of the night is it?" He said, "When half the night has passed until the remaining third."
ai.seo_question: What is the best time for night prayers and supplications to be answered?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the period between the middle of the night and the final third as a prime time for *Qiyam al-Layl*, emphasizing the responsiveness of divine supplication during these quiet hours. In Shia scholarly tradition, this aligns with the concept of *Witr* and the spiritual potency of the pre-dawn hours, where the veil between the earthly and divine realms is considered thinnest. The guarantee of acceptance underscores the merit of consistent night worship as a means of drawing closer to Allah.
